body:
Hi @maxrem thanks for reporting this. It looks like we throw this error if the S3 SDK completely fails to execute the API request (doesn't even attempt it for some reason) and thus we unexpectedly see this exception.
I looked through a lot of logs on our end and could not find a single instance of this failure. I can and will fix this code to not throw a null pointer exception but I think there is a deeper reason for why this is failing on your end. 

Maybe look into the logs to see if there's any failures logged from the S3 SDK before getting to this line?

issue.title: Cleanly Handle S3 SDK Exceptions in Request Counting

labels.name: :Distributed/Snapshot/Restore
labels.description: Anything directly related to the `_snapshot/*` APIs

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
It looks like it is possible for a request to throw an exception early
before any API interaciton has happened. This can lead to the request count
map containing a `null` for the request count key.
The assertion is not correct and we should not NPE here
(as that might also hide the original exception since we are running this code in
a `finally` block from within the S3 SDK).

Closes #61670
